answers.explanation: The writer mocks the Nigerian obituary culture and its exaggerated praise of the dead, which is a satirical tone.
The passage defines mortuary stylistics as the study in the art of eulogizing the dead.
The passage suggests newspapers would make a loss without the revenue from obituaries.
The passage says Nigerians value their dead greatly, which explains the popularity of obituaries.
The passage is about the white man's influence on Umuaro's customs and religion.
The speaker says the people are friendly with Okperi, so they are friends.
The speaker says the white man has come and that the people will not escape him, so they must accept him.
The speaker says the people will not heed his warning, so the words make no impression.
Unachukwu speaks as an elder with experience of travel and of the white man's power, showing he is wise through experience.
The manager's pointed remarks and the secretary's defensiveness show a strained relationship.
By saying he would not describe the secretary as inefficient, the manager implies he is dissatisfied with the secretary's performance.
The manager says the secretary should have supervised the job to ensure the cleaner carried out the instructions.
The secretary says he will not do the cleaner's job, showing an attitude of blaming the cleaner.
The manager says he will not forget the secretary allowed a meeting in an untidy room, so he holds the secretary responsible.
The passage says the firebrand was carried to preserve a flame during journeys.
The passage says the torch may well have developed from the firebrand.
The passage mentions warmth, light and travelling, but does not mention cooking, so man was least concerned with cooking.
The passage says a lighted reed was floated in a vessel containing fat.
The passage says making fire was laborious, so early man had to preserve the flame he had made.
The author says electronic recording shows what happened and who did or said what, overcoming the failings of both memory and writing.
The passage describes record keeping progressing from memory to writing to electronic recording, so it has improved over the years.
The passage describes three stages: mental recording, writing, and electronic recording.
The passage says memory is unreliable because people forget events wholly or in part or deliberately falsify details.
The passage says writing was not entirely free from the shortcomings of memory, so it is almost as unreliable.
